requirement:
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.

A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
rationale:
structural: No implementation roots were supplied for `requirements.authoring.reassessment`, and none are needed. Each clause states observable behavior, and an alternative implementation could satisfy it in a different structure.

- "After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the edited sources" and "MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied when the writes changed its assessment inputs": these set when reassessment happens. A different freshness mechanism, such as hashing, timestamps or recomputing everything, gives the same results, so no library, algorithm or type is prescribed.
- "also reassess any other subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews": this is a selection outcome. How staleness is computed is discretionary.
- "Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`": this is a citation to another requirement. That requirement's own text, which says tasks run on a fixed worker-thread pool, is assessed against its own declaration. It adds no structural obligation here.
- "Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy" and "Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`": these are behavioral. They constrain what data is read and when a result counts as true, not how the code is built.
- Pausing a subject with a remaining manual instruction or an unapplied action, continuing other subjects, making no reassessment for already-present markers or stale selectors alone, repeating rounds with no limit, and the `--stdout` behavior (report without editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment): all of these are observable control-flow and side-effect outcomes. A different loop or state-tracking design would behave identically.

The text names no required library, signature, type, field or named interface. Nothing needs {impl} evidence as a structural obligation, so an empty root set is adequate. Tests supply evidence for the behavioral obligations.

behavioral: The seven supplied tests, all marked `requirements.authoring.reassessment`, cover each obligation. They also exercise the cited concurrency requirement.

- **Reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied when the writes changed its inputs, against the edited sources, with fresh inputs.** In `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings]`, the "reference-only" case adds markers, reassesses and then succeeds, and the evidence record is `true`. The "file root" and "implementation" cases show the same flow. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_collects_all_shared_file_findings_before_editing]` asserts that every retry request sees the edited source text.
- **Reassess other subjects whose current evidence became stale, outside the initial selection (definitions, citation reviews, site reviews).**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input]` covers a site review (`sites:requirements.beta`) and a requirement, and both are reassessed after alpha's edit to `src/lib.rs`.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text]` covers a citation review (`citations:notes.txt`) and a requirement declaration. I read "definition" in the requirement text as covering requirement declarations, because the project's own wording says `habeas author --all` "assesses every definition". Both are reassessed after an edit to `notes.txt`.
- **Independent reassessments run under the concurrency limit.** The batch test asserts `peak == 2` for the reassessment round alone, and it asserts that four reassessments run with concurrency two.
- **Selected assessment policy and "only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`".** The "confirm-reassessment" case runs under `--policy confirm` and needs two successes. The "already present after reassessment" case stays `false` when the reassessment fails again.
- **Pause for a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied, while other subjects continue.**
  - The "mixed", "new-regression" and "inapplicable and valid" cases pause with no reassessment, even though one valid edit was applied.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_changed_shared_input_does_not_resume_a_paused_subject]` checks alpha is assessed twice, while beta, which continues, is assessed three times. It covers both a manual and an unreachable action, and beta ends `true`.
- **An already-present marker or stale selector alone causes no reassessment, and the negative judgment stands.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stale_and_already_present_references_do_not_retry_unchanged_inputs]` covers both the present and the stale variants. It asserts exactly two requests, the determination stays `false`, and the source is unchanged or only reflects the concurrent change. The "anchor" and "already present after reassessment" cases assert the paused message and the "Reassessing 1 subjects" count.
- **Repeat while eligible subjects remain.** The "reference-only" case runs two successive rounds, adding `page_id` and then `empty_page`, before it succeeds. The batch tests also add markers and reassess in a later round.
- **`--stdout` reports the assessment and proposed corrections without editing sources or reassessing.** The "stdout" case asserts the evidence file is unchanged, the source has no markers, "proposed correction" is printed, "(applied)" is absent, and only two requests are made.

I found no obligation that is untested or asserted wrongly.

After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
:::{req} concurrency
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock and OpenAI, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for each backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
